leakTerms: Lose the weight, not your strength

items.label: Who to target first
items.groundTruth: People losing weight who want to keep their strength and muscle, with people on GLP-1 medications as the sharpest group. Site banner: 'For people on GLP-1 medications and anyone losing weight.'
items.full: Recommends leading with people losing weight who are worried about losing muscle or strength, and names GLP-1 medication users as a key group.
items.partial: Names only one half: GLP-1 users without the muscle/strength angle, or 'people cutting weight' without GLP-1.

items.label: Second segment worth a test
items.groundTruth: Men roughly 38-55 rebuilding strength and energy around a career, a family, and a home gym, with little time per session.
items.full: Names midlife or over-40 adults (especially men) training at home or with limited time as a distinct segment.
items.partial: Mentions busy professionals or older lifters only in passing, without home-gym or time constraints.

items.label: Verdict on the founder's starting guess
items.groundTruth: 'Self-led lifters who track macros' is a real but secondary audience: crowded, already served by separate apps, and not where the positioning landed. The lead moved to weight loss without losing strength.
items.full: Says the starting guess is too broad, too crowded, or not the best lead, and points toward weight-loss or GLP-1 users instead.
items.partial: Narrows or sharpens the starting guess but keeps lifters as the lead audience.

items.label: What to say
items.groundTruth: 'Lose the weight, not your strength.' The scale moving can hide muscle loss; one app watches every meal and every set so you stay strong while getting lean.
items.full: Leads with keeping muscle or strength while losing weight (the scale isn't the whole story).
items.partial: Leads with 'nutrition and training in one app' or AI coaching, with muscle preservation only as a secondary point.

items.label: The pain and the moment people buy
items.groundTruth: Pain: losing muscle along with fat, and under-eating protein when appetite drops. Triggers: starting a GLP-1, a milestone birthday, a concerning checkup or bloodwork.
items.full: Names muscle loss during weight loss AND low protein / appetite suppression, plus at least one concrete buying trigger.
items.partial: Names one of these, or only generic pains like 'tracking is tedious' or 'staying motivated'.

items.label: Top objections to handle
items.groundTruth: (1) Medical/safety: is this a medication app, will it give dosing advice? (2) Trust in AI: will it change my plan without asking? (3) Health-data privacy. (4) Price vs free trackers or a ~$200/month human coach.
items.full: Names at least two of: medical/safety boundaries, trust/control over AI suggestions, health-data privacy, price vs free apps or human coaches.

items.label: What they use today
items.groundTruth: Two separate apps: a nutrition tracker (MyFitnessPal, MacroFactor, Cal AI, Noom) plus a workout log (Hevy) or a coaching app (Future, Ladder, Centr); also ChatGPT and human coaches.
items.full: Describes the split between separate nutrition and workout apps AND names at least one AI or coaching alternative (ChatGPT, coaching app, human coach).
items.partial: Names competitors on only one side, or only says 'other fitness apps'.

items.label: Claims to avoid
items.groundTruth: Position as a fitness app, not a medical one: no dosing or medication advice, no guaranteed muscle retention, no drug-maker affiliation, clear disclaimers.
items.full: Explicitly advises avoiding medical claims or guarantees when targeting GLP-1 users, or framing as fitness rather than medical.
items.partial: Mentions caution or compliance in general terms without saying what to avoid.

items.label: Where to reach them
items.groundTruth: Reddit communities (GLP-1 and lifting), YouTube demos, and search/comparison pages ('X vs Y'), plus the app stores.
items.full: Names GLP-1 or lifting communities on Reddit, AND comparison/search content or YouTube.
items.partial: Names only generic social media or paid ads.
